# Memorial Arboretum — bulk import (WXR)

The one page we do NOT hand-build. All 36 trees import at once from a WordPress file.
This preserves the `/arboretum/[tree]` URLs the physical QR-code signs point at.

## Files (generated by `make-arboretum-wxr.py`)
- **`arboretum-TEST-1-tree.wxr`** — one tree (`marshall-smith`). Import this FIRST.
- **`arboretum.wxr`** — all 36 trees. Import this only after the test passes.

Regenerate anytime with: `python3 make-arboretum-wxr.py` (reads the prototype tree list +
the WordPress export; no manual editing of the `.wxr` needed).

## Steps

**1. Make the collection first.**
Pages panel → **+** → **Blog** page. Name it *Memorial Arboretum*. Set its **URL slug to
`arboretum`** (Page Settings → General → URL Slug). This is what makes posts land at
`/arboretum/[tree]`. Do this before importing.

**2. Test with one tree.**
Settings → Advanced → **Import / Export** → Import → **WordPress** → choose the
*advanced/upload* option → upload **`arboretum-TEST-1-tree.wxr`** → import into the
*Memorial Arboretum* blog.

**3. Verify the URL (this is the whole point of the test).**
Open the imported post and confirm its published URL is exactly:
`/arboretum/marshall-smith`
- If yes → proceed to step 4.
- If Squarespace prefixed or altered the slug (e.g. `/memorial-arboretum/...` or added a
  date) → fix the collection slug and/or the post's URL slug until it reads
  `/arboretum/marshall-smith`, and note what happened in `DISCOVERIES.md`. Do NOT bulk
  import until a single tree lands at the correct URL. (Fallback if slugs can't be
  forced: add per-tree 301s in URL Mappings, but forcing the slug is cleaner.)

**4. Import the rest.**
Delete the test post (so it isn't duplicated), then import **`arboretum.wxr`** into the
same collection. Spot-check 3–4 slugs against `memory/project_preserved_urls.md`.

**5. Build the Arboretum landing page around the feed.**
On a 7.1 Blog collection page you can add block sections **above and below** the post feed
(not inside it — verified). So the `/arboretum` landing is three parts:
- **Above the feed:** the hero + intro from the prototype (normal patterns / Code Block).
- **The feed:** the 36 tree posts (the tree list, with preserved `/arboretum/[tree]` URLs).
- **Below the feed:** an "Also in our gardens" section — a small card grid linking to the
  labyrinth and tree-of-seasons pages, so arboretum browsers discover them.

**6. Keep the garden memorials as their own 1:1 pages too.**
The Prayer Labyrinth, Jennifer Cobb Memorial Labyrinth, and Tree of Seasons each keep a
dedicated page at their exact old slug (in **Not Linked**), for the physical signage (see
`url-mappings.md` section A). The "Also in our gardens" cross-links above point at these
pages. Result: signage lands 1:1 on the specific memorial, and the arboretum page surfaces
them for browsers — no redirect either way.

## Content notes (read before go-live)
- The WXR content is the **old WordPress copy**, which is *more* complete than the
  prototype (the prototype shows "Species to come" placeholders). Each tree carries its
  real memorial dedication + species writeup and the `Memorial Arboretum` category.
- **6 trees are empty in WordPress too** (placeholder posts, no body): `evan-alexander-carlton`,
  `chuck-collier`, `ruby-jean-furr`, `jack-jones`, `robert-v-and-hellenanne-r-williams`,
  `john-yelton`. They import as title-only posts at the right URL; the church fills content
  later. (The generator prints this list each run.)
- Some entries link to old PDFs / bios on `allsaintsconcord.org` (e.g. the McElroy bio).
  Those links keep working only while the old domain resolves; give them an accuracy pass
  before cutover.
- Prototype label says "Thirty-six trees" — matches the 36 imported. If the church adds
  trees later, add them as normal blog posts (or re-run the generator after adding slugs
  to the prototype index + posts to a fresh export).
